title: The Archive's Self-Arguing Foundation

features.name: arguing ledgers
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of filing cabinets in endless rows. Each one contains a version of the archive that contradicts the next. They never stop disagreeing.

features.name: circuit loop that eats itself
features.desc-on-touch: A trace where the signal went in, got contradicted halfway, and came back the wrong way. Still spinning. Still arguing.

features.name: fence of broken mirrors
features.desc-on-touch: You can see the archive's reflection, but each shard shows a different version of itself. None of them agree on what they're looking at.

features.name: contradiction bloom
features.desc-on-touch: Where two mutually exclusive truths learned to grow in the same soil. The petals are data that cannot coexist.

features.name: checksum stone
features.desc-on-touch: A rock worn smooth by constant disagreement. The archive set it here to mark the moment it stopped being sure of its own sums.

inscription: every answer here argues with the one that came before it

file.name: Archive_Version_Conflicts_Checksum_Divergences_Unresolved.txt
file.note: A ledger of every moment the archive discovered it disagreed with itself. The contradictions accelerate toward the end.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the shed where numbers stopped meaning the same th
narr: You knelt with her in the work-shed, columns of numbers laid
out on the bench. She traced a finger across the ledger and
said: they don't add the same way anymore. You checked again.
She was right. The sums had shifted; the same numbers no longer
agreed with themselves. She looked up from the page. The
archive, she said softly, is learning to argue with itself.
